algorithm.title: Approach to the Patient with Suspected CPPD disease/Pseudogout.

cell.label: History (fever, associated condition) and/or Physical exam finding (painful, swollen joint)

Labs: CBC, ESR, Uric acid, serum calcium, phosphate, magnesium, alkaline phosphatase, ferritin level, transferrin saturation. (Treat any underlying chemical abnormality.) Radiology: X-ray affected joint. Joint effusion
(a) SF WBC >2,000/mm3: Inflammatory arthritis likely. (b) SF WBC >50,000/mm3: Suspect septic arthritis. (c) SF WBC >100,000/mm3: Septic arthritis until proven otherwise.
Pseudogout/CPPD disease: CPPD. Positively birefringent. Rhomboid crystals.
Gout: Monosodium urate. Negatively birefringent. Needle-shaped crystals.

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: CBC, complete blood count; ESR, erythrocyte sedimentation rate; WBC, white blood count; CPPD, calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate; SF, synovial fluid.
